The '''Rimbaux system''' was located in the [[Halthor sector/Legends|Halthor sector]],<ref name="EAOC" /> a part of the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] portion of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Rimbaux [[Star system/Legends|system]] was introduced in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], which placed it in grid square M-6.<ref name="TEA" /> The name of the system built upon the mention of the location [[Rimbaux Four]] in the short story "[[Musings of an Ithorian]]," which was included in the [[1993]] book ''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]'', a publication that combines creature designs and photographs from various projects of [[George Lucas]], creator of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' franchise, with original text by [[Bob Carrau]]. In the story, an [[Unidentified Ithorian (Rimbaux Four)|Ithorian]] briefly describes their life at Rimbaux Faur after undergoing metamorphosis from the stage of a [[Pupa/Legends|pupa]].<ref name="Monsters">{{StoryCite|story=Musings of an Ithorian|book=Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas}}</ref> [[Lucasfilm]] employee [[Leland Chee]], who maintains the [[Holocron continuity database]], has indicated that information contained in ''Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas'' is [[Canon|non-canonical]] with respect to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity.<ref name="Chee">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=690#14724917|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-05-03|time=5:45 PM|quote=And is information from Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas canon? Unless referred to by a source that is in-continuity, the information is non-continuity.}}</ref>
